title: Allied Health Scholarships: Find Help Funding Your Healthcare Training
summary: This guide covers scholarships for aspiring allied health students and how you can improve your chances of winning them.
body_markdown:
[Allied health covers](https://www.stepful.com/post/what-is-allied-health-guide-to-careers) more than 200 healthcare careers that support patient care but are not doctors, nurses, or dentists.


Though training is quick and affordable compared to becoming a doctor, for example, there are still costs associated with getting trained and certified for these roles.


Those costs are often the thing that stops people from pursuing these careers. But scholarships exist specifically for allied health students, including people training for certificate-level roles rather than those that require multi-year degrees.


Professional associations, hospital foundations, and training providers all fund awards aimed at medical assistants, dental assistants, pharmacy technicians, imaging techs, and more.


This guide covers scholarships open to allied health students and the roles with the most dedicated funding behind them. We’ll also share tips for winning those awards and take a quick look at other ways to cover training costs.


## Allied Health Scholarships at a Glance


Unlike student loans, scholarships don’t have to be repaid, so they should always be where you start your search for school funding.


They are awarded based on financial need, field of study, membership, background, and more.


Here’s an overview of allied health scholarships:

## General Allied Health Scholarships


The scholarships in this section are not tied to a job title. They can help fund your training for many[in-demand allied healthcare roles](https://www.stepful.com/post/most-in-demand-medical-jobs) , so this is a great place to start for any potential student.


A few require membership or specific school enrollment, so check the requirements before you begin.


### Stepful's Scholarships and Grants


- **Organization:**[Stepful](https://www.stepful.com/) , an online healthcare education provider
- **Amount:** Varies by student and program
- **Deadline:** Rolling, no fixed application window
- **Requirements:** A simple, online application


Stepful offers fully online training programs for in-demand healthcare roles, including[medical assistants](https://www.stepful.com/medical-assistant) ,[pharmacy technicians](https://www.stepful.com/pharmacy-tech) ,[radiology techs](https://www.stepful.com/training/radiology-tech) ,[dental assistants](https://www.stepful.com/dental-assistant) , and more.


Our[grants and funding programs](https://www.stepful.com/grants) can cover your tuition if you qualify, and we encourage all our students to research what may be available for them. Through these programs, many students complete healthcare training at no cost.


Stepful partners with organizations that sponsor[free or reduced-cost healthcare training](https://www.stepful.com/post/free-healthcare-training-certifications) and certification.


We also have experience helping students access workforce board money, employer tuition benefits, and[military-related funding](https://www.stepful.com/post/programs-for-military-members-spouses-to-get-free-healthcare-training-certifications) (active-duty, National Guard, Reserve, and military spouses).


Available funding depends on your program, location, and eligibility.


Applying is easy. There is no essay or FAFSA form.


Simply complete an application for a[Stepful program](https://www.stepful.com/programs) to see what scholarships you are eligible for. If you qualify for military-related or workforce board funding, a Stepful adviser will help you do the rest.


[Learn About Our Healthcare Training Programs](https://www.stepful.com/programs)


[Explore Programs](https://www.stepful.com/programs)


### ASAHP Scholarship of Excellence


- **Organization:** Association of Schools Advancing Health Professions (ASAHP)
- **Amount:** $1,000 per recipient; the strongest applicant is also named the Elwood Scholar and receives an additional $1,000
- **Deadline:** June 5 for the 2026 cycle, which has closed, but the application window will open again next spring
- **Requirements:** You must be enrolled and have completed at least one term at an ASAHP member institution. You must be nominated by that institution. You will submit your resume and a one-page essay of no more than 200 words.


The[ASAHP Scholarship of Excellence](https://www.asahp.org/scholarship) goes to students who show strong academic work and leadership potential. The ASAHP is the membership body for allied health schools, and candidates must be enrolled at a member institution.


Students must be enrolled in an eligible entry-level degree program. Associate, bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral programs qualify.


### HOSA National Scholarship Program


- **Organization:** HOSA Future Health Professionals
- **Amount:** Awards are funded by dozens of separate sponsors across specialties including pharmacy, dental, physical therapy, and medical coding. In 2023, HOSA reported 92 scholarships totaling $111,500 from 32 sponsors.
- **Deadline:** April 1, 2027
- **Requirements:** Active HOSA membership through a school or postsecondary chapter.


[HOSA’s National Scholarship Program](https://hosa.org/2024-scholarship-application/) is the largest multi-specialty scholarship network in allied health, open to high school seniors, postsecondary students, and people pursuing a certification. You must be a member of a HOSA chapter through your school.


### CalvertHealth Foundation Allied Health Scholarship


- **Organization:** CalvertHealth Foundation, Prince Frederick, Maryland
- **Amount:** Up to $3,000 per semester, capped at $24,000 total
- **Deadline:** Postmarked by April 15 each year. The 2026 cycle has closed, but the award recurs annually.
- **Requirements:** Transcripts, a resume, a one- to two-page essay, two letters of recommendation from nonfamily members, and an interview with the selection committee. Recipients commit to working at CalvertHealth for at least 24 months, or 12 months if the award totals under $12,000. Break the commitment, and you must repay the money with up to 10% annual interest.


This program helps candidates get the education and training needed to fill critical positions at CalvertHealth in Prince Frederick, Maryland.


[CalvertHealth Foundation Allied Health Scholarships](https://www.calverthealthfoundation.org/Scholarships) can help fund training for radiology technologists, pharmacy technicians, respiratory therapists, medical laboratory technicians, and more. All the eligible roles are listed in the[application packet](https://www.calverthealthfoundation.org/Uploads/Public/Documents/FOUNDATION/Scholarships/2026%20Allied%20Health%20Scholarship%20Application%20Package.pdf) .


Southern Maryland residents get priority, though applicants from elsewhere are considered if they agree to the employment commitment.


### Platinum Educational Group Scholarship Program


- **Organization:** Platinum Educational Group
- **Amount:** Three $1,500 scholarships per cycle, one each for EMS, nursing, and allied health
- **Deadline:** The fall cycle is open Sept. 1 to Dec. 1, 2026. A spring cycle follows each year.
- **Requirements:** Current enrollment in an eligible program, plus a photo, the application form, and a signed photo release. There is no essay.


The[Platinum Educational Group Scholarship Program](https://www.platinumed.com/scholarships) is open to **** students at every level, including those enrolled in high school, vocational or technical, certificate, associate’s degree, and bachelor’s degree programs. The application takes only a few minutes.


### American Medical Technologists (AMT) Scholarship


- **Organization:** American Medical Technologists (AMT)
- **Amount:** Not published
- **Deadline:** Applications open between Oct. 1 and April 1 each year
- **Requirements:** Two letters of reference, a 500-word essay on your career choice, and proof of enrollment or admission. Applicants must be high school graduates (or seniors, GEDs accepted) or current AMT members in good standing. They must be currently enrolled or admitted for the next fall at an accredited institution.


The AMT offers the Registered Medical Assistant (RMA), Phlebotomy Technician (RPT), Patient Care Technician (PCT), and Dental Assistant (RDA) certifications, and more.


The[American Medical Technologists (AMT) Scholarship](https://americanmedtech.org/blog/blog-post/apply-for-an-amt-scholarship) **** is open to students pursuing degrees in AMT-certified disciplines, such as medical technology, medical assisting, dental assisting, phlebotomy, and more.


AMT also runs the[Dorothy “Mimi” Roush Phlebotomy Endowed Scholarship](https://form.jotform.com/AmericanMedTech/rpt-scholarship-application) , which accepts applications year-round from new applicants paying the AMT phlebotomy certification application fee out of pocket.

## Medical Assistant Scholarships


[Medical assistants](https://www.stepful.com/post/what-is-a-medical-assistant) are in demand across the U.S., so several dedicated scholarships and programs can reduce or fully cover your training costs.


### Stepful's Medical Assistant Scholarship


- **Organization:** Stepful, an online health education provider
- **Amount:** Varies by student need
- **Deadline:** Rolling, no fixed application window
- **Requirements:** No essay and no FAFSA. Military, military spouse, and workforce funding have separate eligibility rules.


Stepful’s[Online Medical Assistant Training Program](https://www.stepful.com/medical-assistant) takes five months to complete and includes two live, 90-minute classes per week. The program prepares students to earn the National Healthcareer Association’s[Certified Clinical Medical Assistant (CCMA)](https://www.nhanow.com/certification/nha-certifications/certified-clinical-medical-assistant-(ccma)) credential.


Stepful can help you explore funding options that may reduce or cover your[tuition](https://www.stepful.com/post/free-medical-assistant-training) . We have funding programs[for military spouses and Army and Air Force service members](https://www.stepful.com/post/programs-for-military-members-spouses-to-get-free-healthcare-training-certifications) .


There are also local workforce programs funded by state governments and employer-sponsored grants.


You just have to fill out an application, and a Stepful adviser will help you do the rest.


[Learn about Stepful's 5-Month Online Medical Assistant Program](https://www.stepful.com/medical-assistant)


[Explore Program](https://www.stepful.com/medical-assistant)


### Maxine Williams Scholarship


- **Organization:** American Association of Medical Assistants
- **Amount:** Not published. Ask the association directly before you apply.
- **Deadline:** May 15 each year. The 2026 cycle has closed but reopens each spring.
- **Requirements:** Be currently enrolled in and have completed one quarter or semester of a CAAHEP- or ABHES-accredited medical assisting program with a GPA of 3.0 or higher.


The[Maxine Williams Scholarship](https://www.aama-ntl.org/about/the-maxine-williams-scholarship-fund) **** is the best-established national award for medical assisting students, and it includes a free year of AAMA membership on top of the money. Awards are granted based on academic ability and financial need.


AAMA also runs a newer[Maxine Williams Scholarship in Honor of Crystal Coleman](https://www.aama-ntl.org/about/the-maxine-williams-scholarship-in-honor-of-crystal-coleman--cma-(aama)) for credentialed medical assistants with at least five years of continuous membership who are pursuing further education. Applications for this fund are due Dec. 15, 2026.


### American Medical Technologists (AMT) Scholarship


- **Organization:** American Medical Technologists (AMT)
- **Amount:** Not published
- **Deadline:** Applications open between Oct. 1 and April 1 each year


The AMT offers the Registered Medical Assistant (RMA) credential, among others. The[American Medical Technologists (AMT) Scholarship](https://americanmedtech.org/blog/blog-post/apply-for-an-amt-scholarship) **** is open to eligible medical assisting students.


**>> See More Options:**[Medical Assistant Scholarships](https://www.stepful.com/post/medical-assistant-scholarships)


## Dental Assistant Scholarships


[Dental assisting](https://www.stepful.com/post/what-is-a-dental-assistant-what-do-they-do) is a good career choice with great job security and a decent salary. Most dental assistants do certificate training programs rather than multi-year degree programs, so awards in this category tend to be small.


However, training can be completed in[as little as four months](https://www.stepful.com/post/how-long-does-it-take-to-become-a-dental-assistant) , and many programs are affordable, so these small amounts go a long way.


For example, Stepful’s[Dental Assistant Program](https://www.stepful.com/dental-assistant) prepares you for the Dental Assisting National Board’s Radiation Health and Safety (RHS) exam and takes four months to complete, plus optional clinical hours.


### ADAA/DANB Scholarship


- **Organization:** American Dental Assistants Association (ADAA) in partnership with the Dental Assisting National Board (DANB)
- **Amount:** Between $250 and $1,000 per recipient
- **Deadline:** Oct. 23, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. CT.
- **Requirements:** ADAA membership in good standing. Funds can go toward continuing dental education, DANB exams or certification, ADAA Fellowship or Mastership expenses, or dental conference registration.


[ADAA/DANB Scholarship](https://www.danb.org/career-center/scholarships) is an **** annual award for dental assistants who demonstrate a strong commitment to career growth and lifelong learning. Applications are submitted electronically through ADAA's online platform.


### DALE Foundation


- **Organization:** Dental Advancement through Learning and Education (DALE) Foundation
- **Amount:** Between $250 and $1,000
- **Deadline:** Not published; 2026 awards have been granted; past application deadlines were Jan. 30
- **Requirements:** Open to dental assistants, students, and other dental team members


The[DALE Foundation](https://www.dalefoundation.org/resources/scholarship) runs two scholarship programs: the DANB/DALE Foundation Scholarship and the Liz Koch Memorial Scholarship.


The DANB/DALE scholarship is open to aspiring and early career dental assistants. Funds can be used for DANB exams, review courses, or practice tests.


The Liz Koch Memorial Scholarship is open to dental assistants, students, and other dental team members. The funds can be used for school tuition, course fees, or conference fees.


### National Dental Association Foundation (NDAF)


- **Organization:** National Dental Association Foundation, in partnership with Colgate-Palmolive **‍**
- **Amount:** $1,000 **‍**
- **Deadline:** Applications open March 1 and close at midnight on Aug. 31 each year **‍**
- **Requirements:** Demonstrated financial need, U.S. citizenship or permanent residency, current enrollment in an accredited dental assisting program, good academic standing, and community service involvement. You will need an official transcript, a CV, a professional photo, a 500-word letter of consideration, and two recommendation letters, one from your program director.


NDAF[Dental Assistant Scholarships](https://ndafoundation.org/scholarships/dental-assistant-scholarship/) are awarded to students enrolled in an accredited dental assisting program as part of a long-running[Colgate](https://www.colgateprofessional.com/students-faculty/awards-programs) partnership. The community service requirement is weighted heavily, so give that section of your application real attention.


## Pharmacy Technician Scholarships


[Scholarships for pharmacy technicians](https://www.stepful.com/post/pharmacy-technician-scholarships) are less common than those for other roles here. That may be because some large, national pharmacy chains offer free training to employees.


You can explore these programs through[Walgreens University](https://jobs.walgreens.com/en/career-development#grid-content-1-1:~:text=Ready%20to%20explore,in%20the%20industry.) and[CVS LearnRX](https://jobs.cvshealth.com/us/en/in-store) .


If you're training before you get a job, here are some scholarships and other funding opportunities to explore.


### Stepful's Pharmacy Technician Scholarship


- **Organization:** Stepful, an online health education provider
- **Amount:** Varies based on student need
- **Deadline:** Rolling, no fixed application window


Stepful’s[Online Pharmacy Technician Program](https://www.stepful.com/pharmacy-tech) takes four months to complete and prepares you for the Certified Pharmacy Technician exam (ExCPT) from the NHA and the Pharmacy Technician Certification Exam (PTCE) from the PTCB.


Stepful can help you explore funding options so that your[training is free](https://www.stepful.com/post/cheapest-pharmacy-technician-programs) or as close to free as possible.


We offer need-based grants and work with funding from programs[for military spouses and Army and Air Force service members](https://www.stepful.com/post/programs-for-military-members-spouses-to-get-free-healthcare-training-certifications) . There are also[local workforce programs](https://www.stepful.com/grants) funded by state governments and employer-sponsored grants.


[Learn about Stepful's 4-Month Online Pharmacy Technician Program](https://www.stepful.com/pharmacy-tech)


[Explore Program](https://www.stepful.com/pharmacy-tech)


### AAPT Larry Nesmith Pharmacy Technician Education Scholarship


- **Organization:** American Association of Pharmacy Technicians (AAPT)
- **Amount:** Not published. Contact AAPT directly.
- **Deadline:** Nominations run March 1 through April 30 each year. Applicants hear back by May 15, and checks go out in July.
- **Requirements:** Active AAPT membership, enrollment in an accredited pharmacy technician program with at least 12 completed credit hours, and a C average or better. You submit a personal narrative of no more than two double-spaced pages, transcripts, and a signed letter of support from your program director.


[AAPT Larry Nesmith Pharmacy Technician Education Scholarship](https://www.pharmacytechnician.com/scholarship/) **** recipients are selected on the basis of academic records, recommendation from the program director, leadership and participation in school and community activities, honors, work experiences, and quality and content of the personal narrative.


### ASHP Foundation Midyear Clinical Meeting Scholarship


- **Organization:** ASHP Foundation Pharmacy Technician Advancement Fund
- **Amount:** Meeting registration plus $1,000 toward travel to the ASHP Midyear Clinical Meeting. Up to 15 technicians are selected each year.
- **Deadline:** The 2026 cycle opened July 13 and closed Aug. 13. It reopens each summer.
- **Requirements:** You must be a practicing pharmacy technician at a U.S. healthcare organization that provides or supports direct patient care, and you cannot have attended a Midyear meeting before.


The[ASHP Foundation Midyear Clinical Meeting Scholarship](https://www.ashpfoundation.org/grants-and-awards/scholarships/professional-advancement-scholarships/midyear/technicians) funds 15 pharmacy techs each year to attend their Midyear Clinical Meeting and Exhibition. Money is for conference registration and travel, so this is a professional development award for working pharmacy technicians.


**>> See More Options:**[Pharmacy Technician Scholarships](https://www.stepful.com/post/pharmacy-technician-scholarships)


## Radiology Technologist Scholarships


[Radiologic technology](https://www.stepful.com/post/what-is-a-radiology-tech) has more dedicated scholarship money behind it than any other role in this guide, and nearly all of it runs through a single organization with a single application.


### ASRT Foundation Scholarships


- **Organization:** American Society of Radiologic Technologists Foundation
- **Amount:** Individual awards range from $500 to $5,000
- **Deadline:** Applications are open November through mid-January every year.
- **Requirements:** Active ASRT membership, U.S. citizenship or permanent residency, and residence in the U.S. Entry-level applicants need a 3.0 GPA and at least one completed semester in an accredited radiologic science program.


[ASRT Foundation Scholarships](https://www.asrt.org/foundation/programs/academic-scholarships) **** can be used **** for all kinds of radiologic training, including radiography, radiation therapy, sonography, nuclear medicine, and MRI. You can win only one scholarship per year, and if you qualify for several, ASRT awards you the largest. Every applicant hears back by June 1.


If you are interested in this career but are not a member of ASRT, check out Stepful's online[Radiology Tech](https://www.stepful.com/training/radiology-tech) program. It prepares you to become a certified radiology technologist, and Stepful can help you find funding for training through our[grants and partnerships](https://www.stepful.com/grants) .


## Tips for Winning Allied Health Scholarships


Your scholarship applications don’t have to be perfect. They just have to be honest and on time.


What separates most winners is following directions and submitting before the window closes.


Here are some other tips for winning scholarship awards:


- **Apply for the small ones.** A $500 local award with a short essay can take an hour and draw a dozen applicants. A $10,000 national award may take a full weekend and draw thousands, so think about where you have the best odds of winning.
- **Join the professional association for your field early.** AAMA, AMT, ADAA, ASRT, AAPT, and HOSA all have scholarships for members, and a student membership usually costs far less than a single award pays out.
- **Track deadlines in a calendar the moment you find a scholarship.** Most of these open for a few weeks once a year, and missing the window can mean waiting 12 months for it to open again.
- **Answer the question the application actually asks.** Committees notice recycled essays that drift off the prompt, and it reads as carelessness.
- **Be specific and be honest.** Most of these programs are judged by volunteers reading through stacks of essays that start to sound alike. Being real is one way to cut through.
- **Ask for recommendation letters early.** Ask at least three weeks out, and give the writer your resume and the scholarship description. If you only give the person two days and no context, they are going to give you a very stock letter.
- **Check requirements for GPA and prerequisites.** Some awards have minimum grade or coursework requirements. Make sure you meet them well before applying.
- **Have someone read your materials before you submit.** A classmate, instructor, or program director will catch the sentence that made sense in your head and nowhere else.
- **Create a scholarship folder.** Make a folder with your transcript, resume, essay drafts, and proof of enrollment. After the first application, the rest will take an hour instead of a whole evening.


## Other Ways to Pay for Allied Health Training


While you’re working on scholarship applications, start to research grants, student loans, work-study, and employer tuition-assistance programs. Together with scholarships, they can make your healthcare education more affordable.


Here are some ways to fill the funding gap:


- **Federal aid.** Filing the[Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA)](https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa) shows what you qualify for, including Pell Grants worth up to $7,395 for the 2026-27 award year, and federal student loans.
- **State workforce funding.** The[Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/eta/wioa) funds training for unemployed and underemployed adults through local workforce boards. Healthcare training programs are a common approved use. Find your local board through the[American Job Center locator](https://www.careeronestop.org/LocalHelp/local-help.aspx) .
- **Employer tuition assistance.** Employers can provide up to[$5,250 a year in tax-free educational assistance](https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/irs-updates-frequently-asked-questions-about-section-127-educational-assistance-programs) . Many hospitals, healthcare companies, and pharmacy chains offer tuition assistance to employees in any role. Check with your HR department, even if you’ve never heard of this benefit before.
- **Private student loans.** Treat these as the last option after you have exhausted all other forms of financial aid. They almost always have higher interest rates and less forgiving repayment terms. If you need private student loans,[shop around](https://www.credible.com/private-student-loans/prequal/role) for the best interest rate and make sure you understand how repayment works.


Note that federal financial aid cannot be used to pay for Stepful’s programs. However, other[options for financial support](https://www.stepful.com/grants) are still available.
